texto: Братья Стругацкие хотели чтобы экранизировать свою повесть,  Алексею Герману, режиссер решил снимать «Трудно быть богом» еще в 1968 году, через 4 года после выхода книги. Вместе с Борисом Стругацким они написали первый вариант сценария. В августе Герман получил разрешение на съёмки, но вскоре началась операция «Дунай» — вторжение в Чехословакию войск СССР и других стран Варшавского договора, поэтому режиссеру не разрешили снимать фильм. Производство картины затянулось по причине трудностей с финансированием и сложности озвучания. Когда же финансирование нашлось, снимали картину в 2000 году и закончились в 2006 году. С тех пор, Алексей Герман работал в основном над звуком. К сожалению, он умер в феврале 2013 года, не успев доработать звуковую составляющую. Завершали работу над картиной его сын, Алексей Герман мл., и Светлана Кармалита. Самих же братьев тоже уже не стало. Сама же картина вышла в 2013 г., долго делали эту картину, очень долго, но стоило ли овчинка выделки? А вот и нет, то что Стругацкими использовалось редко и умело, в фильме гипертрофированно до немыслимых масштабов и превратилось в самоцель, идея здесь исключительно одна, мол, все люди коричневая субстанция, коричневая субстанция на них, вокруг них и внутри них, субстанцией люди были всегда и навеки им и останутся, ибо такова их природа, так себе мысль конечно, но это как говорится  “У кого что болит?” Однако донести свою точку зрения можно куда менее блевотными способами, чем строить трёхчасовой фильм вокруг одной банальной идеи залитой литрами жидкой грязи и коричневой субстанцией, иногда вообще закрадывается крамольная мысль, что целью режиссёра как раз и было заснять тонны грязи и коричневой субстанции, чтобы потом посмеяться с того, как люди будут находить в этой смрадной клоаке космической глубины философский подтекст. Разумеется тут же нашлись толпы не быдла объявившие картину гениальной, мол, всё так и есть, только они такие волшебные выходят на улицу, чтобы прикупить очередной IPhone или баночку фуагра, как их тут же окружает грязное вонючее быдло, само собой сами они при этом себя такими не считают, пусть эти товарищи продолжают искать жемчуг в море поноса хоть до скончания времён, нам же как это странно не звучало нужны внятный сюжет, логика, нормальная игра актёров и приемлемая картинка, а не сферичная шизофреничная блевотная ерунда, какой именитый режиссёр её не снимал и сколько бы лет он на это не потратил, король то голый Господа. Адекватной экранизации Трудно быть Богом попросту не существует, если фильм 1989 г. был унылой коричневой субстанцией, то картина Германа это просто коричневая субстанция, причём с большой буквой “Г”, больше сказать нечего и вообще лучше помыть руки, после работы Германа возникает знаете такое неодолимое желание. “I’d rather be happy over liking Hard to Be a God.” - COOP, 2025 I watched this movie almost three years ago and called this dreadful, uncomfortable, and drawn out figurative “snuff film” a masterpiece. Then I never watched it again, and I deeply regret not revisiting it sooner. I have to ask… what the hell did I even see in this movie? A deep character study? Clearly something. I know that not every great film is supposed to be “enjoyable”, but I don’t think a good movie should give me absolutely nothing to enjoy at all, like this one does. Seriously, I could barely even finish it. The only good thing I can say is that the cinematography reflects the movie's tone perfectly. It’s very atmospheric, but that can’t salvage how genuinely uncomfortable it made me feel throughout. And not even in a good, thought provoking way. I got to a scene in the dungeon with only 35 minutes left and just decided to skip to the end… which I know is cheating, but how am I supposed to stay invested in something I already hate watching? Watching this movie again was legitimately one of the most dreadful viewing experiences I’ve ever had. The first time I saw it, I was 15, at a point in my life when I wanted to be a “true cinema nerd” and get into more “absurd cinema.” In doing so, I guess I convinced myself that I loved this movie way more than I actually did. Okay fine; that’s the understatement of the century. The worst thing you can do as a movie fan is convince yourself that you like something you really don’t. I really do want to love these kinds of movies, okay? I think movies like “Stalker” and “Werkmeister Harmonies” are very thought provoking, and masterfully made films that were made with a greater intention than to be slow and enduring for the sake of it. They’re also movies I haven’t seen in a while, but can confirm I’ve seen more than once in less than three years,  and have taken actual time to think down. But this one just feels like an endurance test and never feels like it has anything meaningful to say. It’s nothing more than one big drag of a watch.

A vetítés után 3 nappal koponya MR-re volt időpontom (mármint nem a film miatt, még előtte kaptam). Miközben a gépben feküdtem, jöttem rá, hogy a kettő élmény mennyire hasonlít egymásra. Repetitiv, idegtépő zajok, amelyek hatására az elejétől a végéig csak arra tudtam gondolni, mikor lesz  végre vége. De mindig jött egy következő jelenet kicsit más zajokkal. És köztük egy-két pillanatnyi megváltó csend. Mikor végre azt hittem ennyi volt, közölte a néni hogy "akkor most beadom a kontrasztanyagot" és visszatolt. Ez is megtörtént párszor a moziban. Végül pedig mindkét esetben volt "vészcsengőm", mégsem használtam azt. Látom és elismerem a két dolog értékeit, létjogosultságát. Viszont egyikre sem tudom azt mondani, hogy jó volt vagy élveztem akár egy pillanatát is. Ezért nem tudok a filmre fél pontnál többet adni, holott tudom, hogy közel sem ennyit ér. Ennyire (nem) tudtam befogadni. (Pedig alapvetően nem szoktam bánni, ha fáj egy film, csak inkább ne így.) És mindkettőtől kaptam valamit. A filmtől jó néhány csodálatos képet (a baglyosat imádtam), az MR-től pedig az első letterboxd review-mat.

Posle pročitane knjige odlučila sam i da pogledam film ne očekujući mnogo zbog komentara koje sam videla. Nakon gledanja filma smatram da bi bila uvreda reći da predstavlja adaptaciju istoimene knjige Arkadija i Borisa Strugackog. Prvo skoro pa nemoguće je shvatiti ŠTA je tačno priča koju film hoće da prikaže, tako da ako neko ne pročita kratak opis filma na letterboxdu može samo da gleda smesu blata i svih mogućih izlučevina na ekranu i da se pita koji kurac gleda. Glavni lik don Rumata je u potpunosti drugačije prikazan u odnosu na knjigu. On ovde nema nijednu pozitivnu osobinu, kao lik je plitko prikazan i budući da kao gledaoci nismo nikako povezani sa njim, ne zanima nas nešto previše. Velika šteta jer je u knjizi, kao jedan od naučnika koji je poslat da nadgleda razvoj čovečanstva, prikazan kao osoba koja konstantno razmišlja o svojoj ulozi. Da li treba da ostane posmatrač ili da na neki način pomogne čovečanstvu da krene u pozitivnom smeru razvoja? Tema koja je zapravo i centralna dilema knjige pa zbog toga i takav naslov, ovde nikako nije ni prikazana jer don Rumata se ponaša potpuno isto kao ljudi kojima je okružen. Razgovor u knjizi između Rumate i naučnika Budaha o tome šta bi bog trebalo da uradi da društvo učini boljim , do te mere je učinjen nebitnim, bez supstance i degradiranim jer mu Rumata postavlja ovo pitanje dok Budah piša i nehajno daje odgovore. Posebna tema je režiserov izbor da ovaj svet predstavi kao mesto neopisive prljavštine i splačina, nešto na šta se knjiga ne fokusira, i na kraju ceo film postaje talac blatnjavih vizuala ispunjenih ispodprosečnim likovima. Iskren savet je preskočiti film i dati šansu knjizi koja se brzo čita i postavlja zanimljiva filozofska pitanja ~

So disappointing.. an interesting premise and skillful craft completely ruined by an obsession with punishing the audience through constant filth and a story that seems determined not to go anywhere for the vast majority of its 3 hour runtime. This is likely the most disgusting film I’ve had to endure with little to no reward for it. It’s as though the director instructed everyone to act as vulgar and as uncaring as possible at every given moment regardless of what their character motivations were. Never is an opportunity missed to spit everywhere, physically abuse someone, smear crap on someone’s face, cough up mysterious substances, etc. The main character seems to have no motivation and uses his lethargy to essentially torture those around him and slog through his mud-caked surroundings aimlessly. The movie appears to abandon its premise almost immediately, instead favoring endless grotesque set pieces to test the audience’s endurance. There is a somewhat interesting plot underneath it all and some genuinely impressive cinematography and set design despite how disgusting it is, but digging through the filth just isn’t worth it.

Genuinely can't reconcile this film in my head. On one hand, it's one of the most complexly directed films I've ever seen. Every single decision serves to throw us into the most disgusting pits of hell possible, to relay to us all the textures of this world, to simulate a world that is alive and doesn't care about our presence. On the other hand, none of the directing or scriptwriting serves the viewer. I would say roughly 95% of the movie is genuinely incomprehensible. In my opinion, it's because German wanted us to be as close to all the filth, so meticulously created by production designers, makeup, and casting, as possible, so we spend most of the movie in close-ups, which destroy any sense of where we are, who we're surrounded by, where the characters are going, or if they're going anywhere at all. If there wasn't a voiceover at the beginning, I don't think most people would even get the basics of the plot, let alone its progression. And yeah, it's three hours of structurally repetitive displays of depraved acts combined with a highly naturalistic birthing of all bodily fluids (and sometimes solids) you can name. I respect the attempt, but by doing five genius things, it commits ten unforgivable sins against narrative cinema. P.S. Now I just can't be excited about Eggers' Werwulf, because the despair of the Middle Ages on display here is unreplicable.

J'en attendais beaucoup, une histoire qui me rappelait "Sur le globe d'argent" de Zulawski. J'espérais un côté philosophique prononcé, au final rien n'a de sens, l'histoire n'est absolument pas développée. Tout est centré sur l'ambiance et les visuels du film, qui étouffent le scénario, en plus d'être littéralement tous dégueulasses. Sur tous les plans, on peut voir de la merde, de la boue, des crachats, du vomi, de la sueur, bref tout ce qui est liquide est dégueu est présent partout. C'est l'une des rares fois où je trouve qu'un film a une odeur. C'est l'horreur à regarder, le film transpire, pue, suinte à travers l'écran. Tout ce qui est montré est absolument horrible et ce, sur les trois heures de film, c'est long ! C'est l'effet voulu et c'est entièrement réussi, le côté plastique est extraordinaire et très sensoriel, mais ce n'est pas du tout ce que j'aime et attends, j'ai subi le film. Je n'ai rien compris à ce que je voyais, l'histoire ne sert à rien, il y a très peu de dialogues. Je comprends que ce soit l'oeuvre de la vie du réalisateur, 15 ans de travail dont 13 ans de tournage, sortie après sa mort et terminée par son fils et sa femme, mais ça n'a pas du tout fonctionné sur moi. L'ambiance, les visuels, les décors, les plans, les personnages... Rien ne m'a plu ni touché. Tout m'a fait détourner le regard, souffler et m'a donné la nausée. Impossible d'accrocher et de ressentir quelque chose hormis un néant scénaristique au milieu du dégoût visuel. C'était éprouvant. Je ne veux plus jamais revoir cela, beaucoup trop long et dégoûtant, une grande oeuvre, celle d'une vie, mais l'ambiance insupportable a pris le dessus sur tout le reste.

The Strugatsky brothers should be glad they passed away before this movie was premiered.

Earth scientists on a parallel medieval planet try to coax the civilization towards enlightenment - but you'd never realize by watching it. Whew, what a tremendous slog, both due to the environs and at three hours long.  Oddly watchable in its stark black & white for at least the first hour until the gimmick gets old.  Other reviewers have compared it to the "bring out your dead" scene in Holy Grail for the entire runtime, and they wouldn't be wrong.  The cinematic choreography is admittedly excellent, treating the camera via successive long takes as if an urban man-on-the-street interviewer that gets repetitively walked in front of, blocked by objects, or mugged at by passerby, with numerous instances of characters looking at and addressing the viewer, even if to no point.  Random neanderthal quirk occurs repeatedly at the sides of the screen and in the background, an ongoing ringmaster's freak show that never ends, performed by the ugliest cast director German, who died before the film's release after 13 years of work, could assemble. The plot, if one can be convinced it exists, is barely perceptible beneath the rambling, dada-esque commentary that suggests every character is drunk or suffers dementia.  There are no conversations as such, just dangling statements and exclamations that don't connect to form dialogue.  An hour in, I felt I'd have the same understanding if the TV had been on mute the whole time. If these are truly men of science, they've clearly gone as mad as the inhabitants they study.  The poverty circus atmosphere is mesmerizing because of the continual muddy awfulness (meriting its place in the Dirty Deeds Showdown), as well as the highly-orchestrated stream of constant activity, but everything has an expiration date and this tone never changes.  Credit for maintaining affect ala the recently-seen Rats! , but not nearly as entertaining.  Even the climactic gore, thankfully blanched by the lack of color, didn't rekindle interest. Grossly middle ages filth-fetish stream-of-consciousness from a unique POV that completely buries its story under an incomprehensible adaptation and a wildly overlong runtime.  Interesting briefly for its carny gutter ambience, but it's zero-percent sci-fi and 100% a mess, deliberately and inadvertently.  How this barbaric cacophony derived from a novel, unless it was "Finnegan's Wake," is beyond me.  Grotesquerie alone is not a movie.

I live by one simple rule, and I apply it to every single film I watch: Never let a movie get the better of you. And, so, no matter how boring, repulsive, objectionable (insert any serviceable adjective here) etc…a film is, once I’ve started it, I always finish it…sooner or later. This is a rule that has almost NEVER served me well. Ever. And, yet; here I cling to it, an addict at once unable to stop myself, despite the knowledge that time is exceedingly ephemeral, while also unwilling to allow any artist to ever win in their pursuits of turning me away. And then there’s (Maude) “Hard to Be a God” (which, for the most part of its duration, I kept singing Sheryl Crow’s “Hard to Make a Stand” and exchanging the lyrics) which starts off its three-hour running length with people’s faces being pooped on and somehow manages to lower the bar in perpetuity of its duration. Look, I get what we’re doing here: dumb idiots with a lack of basic common knowledge mistake anyone with any breadth of intelligence for a deity. But….so what? Who cares? Who NEEDS to see this? I mean, actually NEEDS to see it? I give the film points for its spectacular black and white photography (by two cinematographers - Vladimir Ilin and Yuriy Klimenko) and indeed the mere fact that such an oddity (on every single level of its being) exists in the first place. But, by no means, mistake such praise in any universe as recommendation.

Mindenek előtt leszögezném, hogy ezt a filmet egyszer látni kell, mert technikai szempontból lenyűgöző. Mármint abban az értelemben, hogy egy film erre képes. Lehetséges ezt létrehozni, felépíteni, megcsinálni.  Ugyanakkor, felmerül a kérdés, hogy mi végre épült ez a szerkezet, mit akartak mondani vele, mi indokolja? Ugyanis a második óra után nézőként rá kellett jönnöm, hogy a mondanivaló, amire ez a 177 perc épül, nagyon vékony. (Költői kérdésként pedig gyorsan  feltenném, hogy amúgy meg lehet-e úszni bűntetlenül, ha egy moziban háromszor is belemondják a film címét a kamerába?) Értem, az egyes frakciók sosem nyugszanak, és mindig lesznek szürkék, akiknek nem tetszenek a feketék, de amúgy bármikor jöhetnek fehérek, akik meg a másik kettővel akarnak leszámolni. Valaki mindig hatalomra akar kerülni, valakit mindig le kell kaszabolni. Az öldöklés sosem érhet véget. Ez az állítás lehet igaz, de nem kell különösebben okosnak lenni egy ilyen tézis kigondolásához és pláne nem kell 177 perc ennek elmondására. Hogy honnan tudom? Láttam már más filmeket is. A játékidőt esetleg indokolhatja, hogy German ezzel akarja érzékeltetni, hogy a változás sosem következik be és mindig minden ugyanúgy marad: köpködés, hányás, vér, belek, ebéd, majd szarás. Ez a rendezői vízió. Mert ez maximum az. German nem épít világot, csak ügyesen elhazudja azt. A logikátlan dolgokkal telezsúfolt terek ügyesen elhitetik a nézőkkel, hogy amit látnak az egy alternatív univerzum, de igazából olyanok ezek a díszletek, mintha nem lenne ott semmi, mert funkciótlan és felesleges. Ahogy a szereplőket, úgy a nézőt is csak akadályozzák. Egy világ építéséhez szükség lenne arra is, hogy a szereplőket néha lássuk nevetni, tudjuk mit találnak esetleg szépnek, milyen amikor nem ölik egymást, vagy épp nincsenek iszonyatosan bebaszva. Ja, és esetleg a nők és a gyerekek is komolyabb szerephez jutnának, de legalább egynél többnek lehetne szöveges szerepe, amiből jellemet tud építeni magának. És esetleg lassan a környezet és annak szabályai is kibontakozhatnának előttünk. Ezek nélkül csak vízióról, sőt rosszabb esetben üres vízióról beszélünk. A film narrátora ugyan hozzánk vág néhány fogodzkodónak szánt izét, de hogy ki, mikor, mit és hol és miért, az nem derül ki belőle. Szerintem kb. 45 percig nem tudtam ki az a Rumata. De utána sem tudtam, hogy ki kicsoda. Értem, hogy itt cél volt, hogy eltávolodjanak a sci-fi bevett formáitól, csak a film nem indokolja meg ennek az okát. Azt sem, hogy miért kellett ehhez a Sztrugackij-regény? Egy idő után minden csak gimmické silányul. Még a fényképezés egyes megoldásai is (pl.: hogy rendszerint emberek nyúlnak a képbe, tárgyakat lógatnak be stb.), pedig abban van a legtöbb invenció. German egyszerre használja úgy a kamerát, mint egy dokumentumfilmes, meg úgy, mintha egy szereplő lenne, máskor pedig mint egy hideg, objektív külső tekintetet. Ahogy a kamera időnként megjelenik a térben borzasztó izgalmas. Meg az a sok lélegzet elállító kép is, ami van ebben a filmben! Kár, hogy csak az marad meg belőle, hogy mennyire szétkínozza a nézőt, mert nem sikerül mélyre mennie. De lehet, hogy ez az egyik állítása: hogy nem is lehet. De megint csak tippelgetek.

When I first began watching Hard to Be a God , I was reminded of the movies Satantango and The Painted Bird . All three films share a stark, unflinching depiction of bleak, oppressive worlds. They’re all shot in black-and-white, have similarly glacial pacing, and immerse the viewer in the ugly, degrading side of human nature. All three are deeply immersive experience designed to feel relentlessly grim. However, I think those other two films (especially Satantango , which in my view is a great film) succeed far more admirably in their explorations of moral decay and existential despair. (The long running time also feels less punishing with both of those films, despite Satantango being more than twice the length of Hard to Be a God !) There’s a deeper intellectual and emotional resonance in Satantango that Hard to Be a God often lacks, or at least obscures behind its overwhelming grotesqueness. While Hard to Be a God has admirable ideas and themes about societal stagnation and the struggle for enlightenment, it often feels like the film is more concerned with shocking and revolting the audience than with intellectual engagement or philosophical depth. (I understand the film assumes a certain level of familiarity with the Strugatsky brothers' novel and its complex ideas, which does not help a viewer like me, who hasn't read it.) Hard to Be a God is a profoundly unpleasant watch, with practically every shot literally drenched in some combination of filth, blood, piss, and shit. By the end Hard to Be a God reminded me less of Satantango and The Painted Bird and more of two other films that I didn’t particularly enjoy: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom and Fellini Satyricon . (I find Fellini largely overrated, and thought Satyricon was particularly terrible .) All three films seem to put the narrative and intellectual engagement on the backburner in favor of overwhelming viewers with depictions of decadence, barbarity, and chaos. While the filmmakers seem to trust the brutality itself will convey meaningful insight, but does it really tell us anything of substance beyond how awful everything is? In my view, these films are about visceral shock value more than anything else, to the point that they overshadow their own lofty themes and thematic potential. Horrible, miserable, unpleasant, grim… I expected that coming in. That’s why I’m here. And it delivers, in spades. In, quite frankly, too many spades. Yes we’ve done it friends, we’ve found one of the few pretentious film guy arthouse darlings that I don’t like. I wanted so badly to give this a fair shake, but I guess I prefer my bleak cinema a bit more plot or theme driven, and a bit less opaque. There are moments where it all comes together, where the plot carry’s sufficient momentum and the camera work, performances, and sound all work , but those moments mostly come two hours into the film, and are fleeting. Our protagonist is largely indistinguishable from the surrounding populace, just as snotty and brutal as everyone else in this world. Which could work, thematically, but I just can’t grasp what the movie is aiming at. He has all these lines about how hard it is to be a god but the people around him treat him with the same open disrespect as they do everyone else. He seems to belong entirely to this miserable world, not happy in it, but certainly of it , which considering he’s functionally a time traveler is at best odd. There are so many choices being made, intentional choices, choices that feel like they have meaning and purpose and allegorical intent, but I just cannot parse any of it. What it lacks in followable narrative it makes up for with its technical decisions. Having the camera as a physical presence, seen and acknowledged by the characters, is incredibly cool. It emphasizes the physicality of the world, the strangeness, the gross mud and blood and shit. It feels like when you smoke too much and have to go home , right now . It’s tough, because I don’t think the film is bad at all - it’s too purposeful, too singular - and I am glad I watched it, but I doubt I’ll ever revisit it and I certainly wouldn’t recommend it.

You could show me any five minute scene from this movie on its own without context and you could convince me it was part of a greater, complete masterwork of Russian art cinema. Still, immensely admirable of its ability to establish and sustain tone and disgust. Crache dans la boue. Brutalise des gens dans la boue. Pendant trois heures. Par conséquent c’est inévitablement d’une monotonie et d’un ennui inqualifiables… Tout dans ce film est redondance, du même boueux ajouté au même boueux — si ce n’est un notable effort pour produire un crescendo dans la laideur et l’immondice. I wouldn't call it watchable,  though. A movie like this strains my understanding of the medium. As the antithesis of everything I care about in this life, it serves mostly as a warning. It depicts a terrible, terrible world that's probably close to the actual realities of Europe in the Middle Ages we've left behind during the Enlightenment for very good reasons, and asks us to care about the dealings of its inhabitants. The comically slow pace, meagre story that would fit on a torn napkin, and complete lack of remotely redeemable personnel makes these three hours of excruciating mindlessness feel like ten. The ending eschews the book's plot twist in favor of not offering a particular point to the madness at all, except for the fact perhaps that we should be more thankful for the space between us and the world depicted here, which makes the journey to this world even harder to justify. And yet, in the midst of the all the revulsion, there is the beauty of decay. The magic of misty villages full of dirty faces people in dirty clothes, swaying to the hollowness of their collective stupidity. The constant dangling of random objects right in front of and deep looks straight into the camera, like these people are looking for something to save them from their repulsive reality. The frequent moments of comedy resulting from the complete and utter tone-deafness of most conversations that makes Idiocracy sound like the apology of Socrates. I wouldn't recommend this movie to anyone, and yet I feel that Hard to Be A God has a reason to exist as a singular piece of art in a difficult space of its own. Vomit, dicks, violence and all. Dankeschön - Eine persönliche Challenge Hauptrunde: Film 10/10 Ausgewählt von Markus Die Bekanntheit in der Fremde, Konversationen mit dem Unbekannten, sich kennenlernen ohne zu kennen. Genau das sind soziale Netzwerke. Mag man in der Realität auch noch so scheu sein gelingt es den sozialen Netzwerken Kontakte zwischen Menschen zu knüpfen, die sich nicht kennen und in Natura vielleicht auch nicht kennenlernen werden. Ich gebe zu, mein Interesse an sozialen Netzwerken hält sich in Grenzen und dennoch liebe ich nun eines über alles. Letterboxd verbindet Filmliebhaber, regt zu Diskussionen und Austäuschen ein ohne sich der Gefahr der unliebsamen Aufdringlichkeit auszusetzen. Eben weil man auch still bleiben kann, nicht gezwungen wird Kommentarspalten unsicher zu machen. Und so hat man vielleicht mit manchen Usern eine Verbindung ohne dass man auch nur ein einzelnes Mal ein schriftliches Wort direkt gewechselt hat. Genau das mag auch auf Markus zutreffen, über den ich hier gar nicht viel schreiben kann, weil ich nicht viel weiss, aber das ist auch gar nicht schlimm. Ich weiss, dass wir beide eine gewisse Vorliebe für das moderne indische Actionkino hegen und durch seine Auswahl für mich weiss ich auch, dass sich Markus generell nicht davor scheut filmisch über den eigenen Tellerrand hinauszublicken. Nun soll diese Challenge also mit einem Mammutwerk an Film enden, einem Film den ich freiwillig mit an Sicherheit grenzender Wahrscheinlichkeit nie geschaut hätte. Genau das hat aber auch den Reiz dieser Challenge ausgemacht. Sich an den eigenen Sehgewohnheiten kitzeln zu lassen und da ist "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" tatsächlich der eigenwilligste, sperrigste und künstlerischste Film, der mir in den zehn Werken begegnet ist. Dennoch, für ein Gefallen standen die Vorzeichen schlecht. Mit "Stalker", "Mirror" und "Tausendschönchen" hatte ich schliesslich unlängst herausgefunden, dass ich mich vom russischen, beziehungsweise osteuropäischen Experimentalfilm so gut es geht fern halten möchte. Mission gescheitert, denn "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" setzt mit seinen 177 komplett in schwarz und weiss gehüllten Minuten all dem noch die Krone auf. Die Geschichte basiert hierbei lose auf dem Roman "Es ist nicht leicht ein Gott zu sein" von Arkadi und Boris Strugazki aus dem Jahre 1964, welcher bereits 1990 unter deutscher Regie für das Kino adaptiert wurde. "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" entfernt sich aber von der linearen Erzählung, nimmt nur die Grundidee für ein unendlich langes Delirium, welches natürlich an Andrei Tarkowski erinnert. Alexei German sah sich selbst als ähnlicher Filmemacher, nur das Ergebnis seines Epos "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" sah er selbst nicht. Sein gleichnamiger Sohn musste das Werk nach dem Tod seines Vaters vervollständigen. Das Endergebnis hat nun vor allem eine interessante Ausgangslage, die natürlich dem Roman entnommen wurde. Weit entfernt von der Erde gibt es andere Planeten auf denen ebenfalls Menschen leben, allerdings sind diese in ihrer Entwicklung zum Teil weit hinter den Erdlingen zurück. So wurden Wissenschaftler auf diese Planeten geschickt. "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" folgt nun einem dieser Wissenschaftler, der in einer mittelalterlichen für eine Art Gottheit gehalten wird. Daraus entspinnt sich tatsächlich ein faszinieremdes Gedankenspiel. Was wären, wenn Adel und Klerus einst erfolgreich gewesen wären, wenn sie es tatsächlich geschafft hätten jede Form der Bildung zu unterdrücken? Das führt natürlich zum Konflikt mit dem Protagonisten. Er darf nicht eingreifen, ist aber mit dem Wissen gesegnet, welches wir heutzutage in dieser Welt besitzen. Einer Allwissender unter Ahnungslosen. Wie Gott schaut er zu, sieht wie alles entgleitet und in die falsche Richtung läuft. "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" will seinem Titel gerecht werden, lässt das Leben dieser Menschen aus der gebildeten Perspektive als das reine Grauen auftreten. Der Kniff dabei ist, dass der Protagonist eigentlich nur für den Zuschauer steht. Er und das Publikum durchschreiten die gleiche Hölle, sind gleichermassen zum Zuschauen verdammt. Ein Film, der plötzlich verständlich macht warum Gott in der Bibel eine Sintflut nach den Menschen schickt. Gleichzeitig kann man das aber auch kritisch hinterfragen. Ist eine Einmischung wirklich sinnvoll, zwingen wir den Anderen damit nicht nur das auf, was wir für richtig halten? Und wer sagt uns, dass unser Verständnis von Bildung, Gut und Böse wirklich das Richtige ist? Über das philosophisch angehauchte Gedankenspiel hinweg, bleibt "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" vor allem durch die Visualität in Erinnerung. Es scheint als hätte Alexei German extra einen neuen visuellen Stil erfunden um seine Vision dieser Geschichte auf Film zu bannen. Denn das muss man "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" lassen, die Bilder brennen sich gewalttätig in das eigene Gedächtnis. Eine schmuddelige, mittelalterliche Welt, die schmuddeliger und mittelalterlicher wirkt, als in jedem denkbaren schmuddeligen Mittelalterfilm. Die Strassen sind kaum als solche zu bezeichnen, bilden sich eher aus knietiefen Bädern des unerbittlichen Schlamms, regelmässig gewässert durch den unablässlich in Strömen quälenden Regen, welcher das trostlose Dasein mit seiner Nässe in eine unertrgliche Trübniss verwandelt. Die Kamera hält dabei immer drauf, entzieht sich Panoramen, die dem Zuschauer eventuell doch noch eine wohltuende Schönheit bieten könnten, und ergötzt sich an den nahen zerfurchten Gesichtern des Wahnsinns, behängt mit Regen, Schlamm und allen möglichen Formen der Fäkalien. "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" zieht seine Faszination aus diesen Bildern, die einen Schmutz heraufbeschwören, der an der Grenze des Erzragbaren wandelt. Man möchte sich während des Filmes duschen, dieser kalten, nassen und ekelhaften Hölle entfliehen. Man möchte Szenen, wie jene in welcher ein kleiner Junge mit einem Löffel einer entblössten Leiche Kot aus dem Hinterteil puhlt um diesen einer anderen Leiche in den Mund zu stopfen, vergessen bevor man sie überhaupt gesehen hat. Das alles hat seine Faszination, könnte mir aber in dieser Ausführung nie gefallen. Auch weil "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" einen grossen Unterschied zwischen German und Tarkowski, dem ich noch etwas mehr abgewinnen kann, ausmacht. Filme wie "Stalker" und "Mirror" fordern die Zuschauerschaft auf intellektueller Ebene heraus. Man kämpft sich durch den Film um die Botschaft, die Gedankengänge und Ideen greifen zu können, getrieben von der Gewissheit, dass eine erzählerische Brillanz vorhanden ist. Das ist bisweilen entkräftend und frustierend, aber man weiss wofür man sich durch die Filme kämpft. "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" fordert hingehen eigentlich nur die eigene Übelkeit heraus. Die Geschichte an sich ist stattdessen sehr schnell entschlüsselt. Spätestens nach einer Stunde ist dem Zuschauer klar worauf der Film hinauswill, worin das Gedankenspiel und die Ideen bestehen. Daraufhin heisst es nur noch durchhalten. Es gibt keine Sympathiträger, die Figuren sind abstossend, schräg und weinerlich. Die 177 Minuten erschliessen sich somit nur noch als eine Selbstverliebtheit des Regisseurs in die eigenen Bilder. Denn eine Rechtfertigung für die Laufzeit von drei Stunden findet "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" nie, wodurch die Zeit mehr und mehr zur reinen Tortur verkommt. Ich kann die Begeisterung für Filme wie "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" durchaus nachvollziehen, allerdings in keinster Weise teilen. Auch für mich übt dieses Werk eine Faszination aus, doch verebbt diese zu schnell in der mangelnden Aussagekraft. "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" ist eben auch wieder so ein Film, der den Zuschauer aus jeder Pore anschreit er sei Kunst, doch ehrlich gesagt macht er es sich damit zu einfach, nimmt das als Vorwand um weniger leisten zu müssen als andere Filme, um auf keine Konventionen Rücksicht zu nehmen und eine Vision des endlosen Grauens, aus Blut, Gewalt, Armut und Ekel durchzuziehen. Darin kann ich keine Unterhaltung finden, daran kann ich keine Freude finden. Ein Film wie "Es ist schwer ein Gott zu sein" erfüllt mich in jeiner Hinsicht, bietet keine intellektuelle Bereicherung sondern kann sich ausschliesslich als Nervenprobe dahingehend, wie viel Leid man bereit zu etragen ist, beschreiben lassen. Dennoch auch hier der obligatorische Dank an Markus für eine einmalige Erfahrung. Und somit endet der wichtige Teil dieser Challenge. Zehn Filme, die sich als bunte Mischung aus Geheimtipps, Experimentalfilmen und zeitlosen Klassikern entpuppten. Zehn Filme die mir mal weniger und meistens mehr gefielen, mir in erster Linie aber eine erinnerungswürdige Reise durch eire Filmgeschmäcker ermöglichten. Eine Reise die für mich noch nicht ganz beendet ist. Einige von euch nannten noch Ausweichmöglichkeiten, Filme von denen sich mittlerweile nicht wenige sogar in meinem Zugriffsbereich befinden, weswegen ich je nach Lust und Laune noch mehrere dieser Filme abarbeiten werde. Als Bonusrunde, ohne zeitliche Begrenzung, ohne zwingend besondere Reviews und ohne den Zwang wirklich alle abzuarbeiten, sondern nur die, die mich interessieren, oder auf die ich spontan einmal Lust verspüre.

Through a sensory odyssey primarily consisting of what you just know is the colour brown, even though it's in black and white, a look at absolute stagnation where humanity finds itself at a grim evolutionary dead-end if history was to have taken a different wrong turn and come to a dead stop. At the same time, it is hard to imagine how in the admittedly hyper-specific circumstances of asking someone to parody the grimmest, largely humourless (the protagonist gets a finger poked up his nose at one point) Russian art film of religious metaphor largely as rolling around in a giant pigsty that they could imagine, they'd come up with anything too different. As every surface is coated in mud and blood and every sky completed obscured by grey fog with the very distinct roaming camerawork pressing itself right up into it, it's no exaggeration to call this one of the most overwhelmingly filthy movies ever made, turning a world essentially based on our historical past into an almost unrecognisable as human hellscape. You're done with the sound of sinuses by the end of the first fifteen minutes. It is undoubtedly one of those films with such a self-assured textural style that very little else will look like it, and the one primary thing it seeks to get across mixed in of course with the Stalinist critiques of the murder of intellectuals barring all routes for advancement seems to be to ask what a non-interventionist god could even do for a world that humanity has driven into a hole. It shows vignette after vignette of people being dumb and cruel and an observing god who is burned out and exhausted by it, isolated in a world beyond help. It seems to argue that global progress is not guaranteed, that the world is not inevitably destined to get better over time if we just negligently sit back to let it, which in might make this a compelling dark mirror image of a worst possible scenario lest we not work to avoid it if you choose to view it so. By basing its entire being in a three-hour quagmire though of mostly passive observance, it creates a storytelling impasse. Where something like On the Silver Globe might show the maddened cycle of civilisation, this shows through its similarly vivid design the existential flatline where progress is stunted, and it's hard to get away from that being quite boring. Worse still this actually quite straightforward to describe structure and character pitch is delivered incomprehensibly by its actual script speaking in what largely amounts to nonsense and non sequiturs, and these political and philosophical ideas might be actually more palpable if its story wasn't so deliberately obtuse and intent on keeping its world abstract. By the end of the first hour we've basically learned very little about its characters that we're following and its factions and forces, and for the most part for the next two that's where it stays, a contextless tour of a mucky, mucky place. It plods through these various encounters that purposefully don't amount to much as progression is antithetical, and it often comes off bumbling as much as it does horrific, a great realisation of a setting but with thin, ponderous storytelling within it. It's certainly somewhat hypnotic through its pure verisimilitude, but not especially interesting. Definitely a vibe and an achievement, but honestly that should be more moving.

Tratto dall’omonimo romanzo di fantascienza dei fratelli Arkadij e Boris Strugackij, racconta la storia di un gruppo di scienziati terrestri inviati sul pianeta Arkanar, che vive in una specie di medioevo politico, culturale e sociale, con il compito di favorire il progresso, salvando dalla morte gli intellettuali del pianeta. I fratelli Strugackij, maestri della science-fiction sovietica, nel libro, denunciano gli orrori della dittatura e della repressione culturale con un apologo cupo e pessimista che, trasposto ai tempi odierni, può considerarsi ancora valido, perché è applicabile a tutte le dinamiche di potere: “quando al potere ci sono i grigi, prima o poi arrivano sempre i neri”. German ne trae un affresco in uno splendido bianco e nero, con una bellissima fotografia, utilizzando una serie di strettissimi piani sequenza allucinanti, allucinati e folli che gli sono costati 15 anni di lavoro. É un susseguirsi (170 minuti) di merda, sputi, fango, merda, piscio, catarro, merda, animali morti e vivi, sangue, interiora, merda, pioggia, sputi e ancora merda. Eppure è un’opera talmente straniata e straniante (un misto tra Sokurov, Tarkovskij e Cinico Tv) da risultare ipnotica. Praticamente senza colonna sonora, tranne due brevi inserti, suonati dal protagonista con una specie di clarinetto, che si ispirano alla musica jazz. Una menzione speciale va a  Leonid Yarmolnik che è praticamente presente in quasi tutte le inquadrature ed è perennemente zozzo dalla testa ai piedi. A proposito del film, dirà: “Come ogni autentica opera d'arte ci ha regalato l'eternità. E' un film per tutti i tempi, per tutti i secoli. Un film che ragiona su come sia senza senso tentare di ricostruire una civiltà, ma allo stesso tempo come sia impossibile smettere di provarci". Non è un capolavoro, ma vale la pena vederlo anche solo per la parte tecnica.

Undoubtedly a masterpiece of filmmaking. Aleksei German spent the last 13 years of his life crafting this grimy, anti-fascist sci-fi epic, and boy, it is a sight to behold. The scope of this film is beyond belief. I was blown away by the intricacies of its design—every set piece is perfectly staged and framed like a painting, and yet there remains a chaos to it that makes it feel lived in; more documentative than cinematic. This feels like a more rugged companion piece to Żuławski's Silver Globe , both telling tales of Earth-born false messiahs with a similar style and complex production history. The main difference between them is how they get their point across: Żuławski opts to take a more cerebral approach, with his film's visuals acting as a supplement to his prose. German, on the other hand, largely favors the visceral, much more concerned with the potency of his imagery than the context behind it. Unfortunately, it is for this very reason that I much preferred the former. Like I said at the start, this movie is a masterpiece on many levels...but man, without prior context, it's a bit of a chore to sit through. I've never felt quite this lost while watching a movie—without the Wikipedia article for reference, I wouldn't have had a clue what exactly was going on here. Maybe that's intentional? Was I being punished for lack of knowledge on the source material? Condemned to share the lowly serf's ignorant perspective of the film's events? I wouldn't be surprised. I'd actually kind of respect such an inhospitable practice. Regardless of intention, the utter lack of clarity here was a significant hindrance on my overall appreciation. I'm a bit bummed I didn't adore this, but I'm still very glad I watched it. It's an overwhelming cinematic success, and even if the message isn't clear, the artistry behind it speaks for itself. That said, unless I get around to reading the original Strugatsky Brothers story at some point, I have absolutely no desire to ever watch this again.

This is an absolute failure. The film was the poster child for production hell: principal photography began in 2000 and wrapped in 2006, after which Aleksei German spent another seven years struggling to wrestle the footage into shape. He passed away before the premiere, leaving the remaining work to be finalized by his family. "Hard to Be a God" is a killer film: a killer of Aleksei German and a killer of meaning — it is the apotheosis of banality and the vulgar misanthropy of the Russian intelligentsia. Despite the mastery with which certain scenes in this film are shot, I cannot say anything good about it, because as a cohesive work, this film is unconvincing. From the outside, it looks as if a neural network was asked to remake Andrei Rublev in the style of Khrustalyov, My Car! , and it generated a cacophony of coprophilic scenes. Many foreigners unfamiliar with the context, or who haven't read the Strugatsky brothers' novel, think they're missing some 'great meaning' in the film, but I assure you — they haven't missed a thing. There are no hidden, secret meanings, details, or nuances in this film – it's a crude, straightforward "rape" of the viewer, delivering the most banal message about the animalistic nature of man (stretched out over three hours).

This film is 3 hours of absolute mayhem and carnage. The film is about a group of humans who get sent to another planet with humans, but these ones are stuck in the Middle Ages basically. So the Earth humans have to integrate themselves with the populous and make sure that they are able to get through these dark times. We follow one of these Earth humans know has ‘Don Rumata’. At no point did I feel like the Don Rumata was doing his job and why he came to the planet in the first place. To help this civilization evolve. It felt like he was just abusing everyone and being a complete menace. He takes method acting to a whole new level 😂. It’s quite clear that he has immersed himself so much that he’s really living the lie. Leonid Yarmolnik, the actor who plays Don Rumata, gives a phenomenally true and outlandish performance. He was great. I could see an argument for watching this with subtitles OFF. They provided basically no help in terms of what was happening. The only upside is that quite a bit of the dialogue is funny and some of it can be surprisingly profound. Honestly I got more understanding of the story from one of the old Lego games, where there’s no dialogue and just grunting. It’s like the actors were told the beginning and the end of a scene and then told to just improvise the rest. To be honest, to begin with, it was a tough watch because of how nonsensical it is. The production is crazy good and completely immersive. There are few films that are at this level in terms of that aspect. It’s muddy and mucky everywhere, everyone is covered in piss and shit. Every part of the film feels so alive. As if they really created a fully fictional medieval village and told all the extras to go about their jobs whilst the film was happening. There’s a part where someone’s guts get spilled out and then his whole chest comes away and you see a still beating heart. Some guy literally gets dragged by a horse during a scene. There are also so many times where someone will just get shat on midway through a scene 😂 The film is shot in a documentary style. The amount of times a scene will be happening and some dude will just walk across the frame, looking directly down the lens the whole time. So funny. Because of the documentary hand held style the camera work is really interesting. The camera is constantly moving and it feels like the film has very few cuts. The editing is pretty good in that regard too. There isn’t really any worrying about if something is slightly obscuring the shot or if the lens is covered in blood or crap. That being said though, towards the end, during a pivotal scene, someone is blocking the majority of the fame. I think someone from behind the camera calls out (not heard) the actors look, wait (someone says wait), the person blocking the frame moves slightly and then the actors continue with the scene. Like nothing happened 😂. I watched this in two sittings. I don’t know whether the second half is better or, if me having a sleep made me enjoy it more. Honestly though, once you just accept it for what is it, there’s so much humour in its wackyness and uniqueness. Below is just a few of my favourite quotes/passages of dialogue from this film: “Don Rumata, the empires best swordsman. 186 duals but not a single kill. Only their ears. 372 ears in total.” “Maybe the Abyss belched you out? Maybe you’re the son of god?” “The fact that I’m talking to you… doesn’t necessarily mean we’re having a conversation” “Don’t get mad Don. Have a potato” - “What would you do if you were a god?” - “I wouldn’t have any problems urinating” (Don proceeds to pour out his water flask to help the man - the man later urinates on Don) “Creator, if you exist, blow us away like dust or pus. Or leave us to rot like we are. Destroy us all. Destroy everyone.” “Get out, everyone. I’m going to wash my arse” “I saw you blowing snot today” “If you write about me, and you’ll probably have to… write that… it’s hard to be a god”

My main takeaway was how the observant and brutally honest camera with its fourth wall breaks felt like a means of having us feel like an observer to this world and the misery and depravity around us and having us being unable to do anything to change things, this felt like a way of using the language of cinema to evoke in us that sense of powerlessness and oppression many people were feeling.

383/500 Aleksei German’s Hard to Be a God is an immersive and miasmic experience that chooses textural storytelling over traditional narrative. Within the first few minutes, excrement has been thrown, and you must decide for yourself whether you’re in or out. The filth doesn’t end there: German’s entropic odyssey festers with pestilence, decay, rot, and offal, all caught within the claustrophobic framework of Ilin and Klimenko’s somnambulant cinematography. Hands in the camera; piss, shit, and spit just being thrown at you for three hours straight—it’s a complete indifference to the audience and to the film’s subjects. But that indifference is the point. Ilin, Klimenko, and German visualize an authoritarian society where there is no personal space; life clambers on top of itself, everyone preying on everyone else just to survive. It’s a direct reflection of the Stalinism that German’s family lived through. Hard to Be a God is constantly reminding us that there is no dignity in authoritarian societies. Rumata starts the film as a passive observer, believing he can watch the cruelty and stupidity around him without joining it, hoping to influence society through behavior modification. By the end, he realizes he can’t, and that he’s as guilty as everyone else of contributing to the moral rot of Arkanar society. In a world devoid of purpose and meaning, ennui and cruelty consume everyone and everything; and passivity becomes its own sort of violence.

I came for the interesting premise, but stayed for the prolonged claustrophobia, snorts and farts, and depravity. Three hours full of shots with meat hooks or ropes hanging in the middle of the screen, incredibly oddly crowded rooms and fast-paced, short dialogues. All the while you're unable to make sense of all that's happening, and are entertained with beautiful photography and unique cinematography that seems to deliberately break every rule of film. This is an incredible experience, unbelievably perplexing and even funny. This is close to a masterpiece.

Unceasingly filthy.  Probably the dirtiest, grossest movie that I've ever seen, and I've seen some pretty gloopy movies.  Everyone and everything is muddy.  People are spitting and blowing their noses and pissing on each other.  Lots of poop and dead animals.  But the part that really sells it is how every shot is so tight and claustrophobic with very few breaks.  You really feel like you're getting gloop rubbed on your face as you watch.  And in that respect, I found the film very successful.  It's an effectively gross film, which is clearly done to make some point.  Some of the finer points are surely pretty muddy, but I think I got the general idea.  That said, I'm not sure how much of this one I'd be able to parse at all without having read the book before watching.  I also don't think that the way that the film updates the novel's ideas to apply to post-Soviet times work as well as the original ideas.  They certainly make it much bleaker, and the book isn't exactly happy or hopeful.  Pretty much everything is filth and hopeless in this version.  It's pure stagnation.  Pretty much all of the good intelligentsia and revolutionary stuff and even references to the advanced earth and its science from the book are cut out or at least it's very much in doubt.  It's a pretty cynical version of the story, at least.  This is not so much a descent into fascism, as an inert and inescapable despotism.  I also think that it kinda wallows in that cynicism without adding a ton of depth to the idea in its long runtime - probably would have been fine with a a decent amount cut out.  The book has more nuance for me by entertaining a positive possibility.  That said, I do like that someone made such a strange film like this.  It's always fun to see something effective and original in eliciting a reaction from the viewer.  The cinematography is very well done, even in its ugliness.  So, I'm glad that I watched it, but I'd definitely recommend reading the book first and knowing what you're getting into before sitting down with this film.

C'est l'exemple type d'un film qui mise davantage sur l'expérience et l'atmosphère que sur l'intrigue ou la structure. Si je n'avais pas lu le synopsis, je n'aurais même pas compris que le protagoniste venait d'une autre planète. Le reste du récit tourne autour de seigneurs qui en trahissent d'autres et d'une histoire d'élimination de l'intelligentsia, mais cela m'a finalement peu importé. Ce n'est certes pas un film facile à regarder, mais son audace pure et les moyens déployés pour créer cette atmosphère poisseuse sont impressionnants en soi. Je ne sais même pas comment ils ont réussi à le réaliser (y avait-il seulement un scénario ?), et c'est ce qui lui confère une qualité fascinante, faisant de lui une œuvre puissante dans l'ensemble. Parfois, un film cherche simplement à offrir au spectateur une expérience viscérale, presque primitive. C'est précisément pour cette raison que j'ai adoré *Il est difficile d'être un dieu*. Si, en tant que spectateur, vous ne cherchez pas à décortiquer le symbolisme à tout prix et vous laissez simplement porter par l'expérience, l'absence d'intrigue véritablement construite ou développée contribue en fait à accentuer cette atmosphère charnelle, confuse et volontairement brouillonne. À mon sens, c'est là tout l'intérêt du film : s'immiscer sous votre peau. Le film existe presque comme une divinité maudite : terrible dans sa réalité, écrasant par son immensité, mais porteur d'une vérité intemporelle, unique en son genre, qui exige d'être explorée par tous les sens, aussi bien terrestres qu'éthérés. C'est un film qui honore le cinéma dans sa forme la plus pure et la plus concentrée, affranchi de toute contrainte narrative et célébrant une imagerie aussi obsédante que sublime. L'univers oppressant et pourtant impressionnant dans lequel se déroule l'action est rendu avec une maîtrise telle qu'il en devient répugnant, alors que l'on patauge dans la crasse, la fange, la boue, la merde et la pisse.

Yikes. Really tough watch. Prefacing with this before any thoughts: approach with a LOT of caution. I have a pretty strong stomach with movies, I was squirming a lot in this one. Hard to be a God is equal measures Bela Tarr and Andrzej Żuławski, but just lathered in feces and mud. It takes on a really bold idea with an even bolder stylistic approach. It’s completely soaked in filth, with sewage oozing out of its every breath. It uses atmosphere as its primary language, something I greatly respect, and respect this movie I certainly do. I think its runtime makes sense when you consider its style and pace, and I love this director’s sentiment of making this film his entire life. That said, I believe the narrative tends to get lost in this world which we really do sit in. Unfortunately I believe the world is well established quite early on, and we continually come back to just showing off how well crafted it is which makes for a really rocky experience trying to follow the plot. To return to a positive, everyone on this set understood the project entire, and no one on screen at any given moment isn’t giving their absolute all to the spectacle. It’s audacious, it’s sick, and it’s completely unrealistic, but the sheer love of the craft and commitment from everyone involved pulls off the impossible and they bring this thing to life. For that I tip my hat, and applaud this endlessly. It’s flawed, but it’s an absolute labor of love, and I respect it wholeheartedly. It made me very queasy, but that was completely the intention. Really wild filmmaking, very evidently inspired, and something you almost can’t help but feel in awe of.

Paradoxalmente, uma das reprentações mais acuradas da Idade Média depois de "Andrei Rublev" (Tarkovsky, 1966), "É Difícil ser um Deus" (Aleksei German, 2013) não é diretamente sobre o medievo terrestre, mas sim o de um outro planeta chamado Arkanar. Alegoricamente, é também sobre o terrestre, claro. E não é nada agradável de se ver; ao invés de romantizar esse período da História humana, German retrata-o como um antro de sujeira e iniquidade. É necessário um notável esforço de atenção para compreender o que se passa, pois captamos apenas fragmentos. Ao invés de um plot tradicional, com fases narrativas bem delineadas e personagens imbuídos de motivações claras, o diretor propõe uma experiência sensorial. Um pouco como no cinema de Béla Tarr, somos postos diante de um continuum em que o lento desdobrar do tempo tem de ser sentido, ao lado da materialidade palpável de lugares e pessoas. Em planos longos, a câmera flutua pelas ruas e interiores de casas, criando um efeito de imersão no universo camponês mais lúgubre que você já viu. São três horas que não passam nada rápido, mas que ficam gravadas na memória.

I finished the book a few weeks ago and was heartened to hear there was a film adaption. A very grim 3hr long black and white film adaptation in the Russian of the original book. its less of an adaptation and more of an endurance test.  And while it is definitely a great film its almost impossible to recommend. It maybe does feel more at home in a gallery than a kino. Its a fantastic film but it highlight certain inefficiencies of adaptation. The tactile horror of Irukan is established here and there with a sentence in the book. Film needs to reiterate and restate the mud and shit and piss and toothless death again and again and again. Any respite from it changes the world the film is set in. The endless pig ignorance; the vulgarity the stupidity, the mud, the incessant rain. The endless sniffing, and smearing, and spitting. I've never seen so much implied stink on screen. It reminded me of a lot of an Irish music festival. Its a 3 hour long hilarious dance, full of interesting blocking and interaction with framing and rhythm. Objects and people come in and out of frame, emerge and reemerge at different depths. A space in the background opens up and is immediately.  sullied with a bucket of horseshit. It could be argued that this is a VIBES movie and the VIBES are bad. Its quite unintelligible and if I had not read the book I would probably have had little to no idea what was going on. A long Eastern European tradition of taking quite pulpy literature and converting into lengthy and obtusely beautiful slogs. It reminded me a lot of On The Silver Globe in terms of its relative illegibility, but whereas Silver Globe is compelling in its beauty, Hard to Be A God is Hard To Be A Good Time. Its not a good time; but it IS a fascinating piece of art. And while I think adaptations are usually stupid because most good art is perfectly formed for the vessel it was delivered in, HTBAG revels in its own mediums strengths and shortcomings. It almost laughs in the face of the idea of an adaptation. It removes the one crucial necessity in adapting a novel like HTBAG; a narrator. So this adaption is avoid of a lot of the swashbuckling that makes the book so entertaining. Even the love story is mutated the edges of recognition. Its such a baffling film. Why is it 3 hours long? The form is part of the joke I suppose. I didn't watch this in a single sitting, and I even fell asleep for chunks of it here and there. I don't think I missed anything too crucial. Its like passing out while somebody repeatedly stamps on your head.

An Earth scientist, ensconced undercover as a demi-god nobleman on the planet Arkanar, which is populated by humans whose development has become stuck in the Middle Ages due to being in the grips of a violently anti-intellectual dictatorship, slowly begins to lose his mind and "go native" as he gets ever more involved in pushing Arkanar into the Enlightenment Age. Or... at least I think that's what the movie is about.  It's difficult to figure out as the film de-emphasizes plot in favor of plunging the viewer into a hellish, shit caked medieval world for 3-hours.  The director's use of documentary-style POV makes you feel like you're constantly in the thick of it as you follow the main character around, getting jostled around by the filthy inhabitants of this world as they grin in your face with idiotic and maniacal smiles.  The effect almost makes it feel like the filmmakers truly traveled back in time to document the toil and drudgery of medieval life. That being said, this movie is a hard, *hard* watch.  What little story that is meted out is difficult to follow, and the sci-fi concept of Earthling observers studying this planet is so downplayed as to be practically non-existent to the plot.  It's hard for me to imagine the main character, and the other Earth scientists, have ever been anything other than Arkanar natives (perhaps that is the point).  Still, some hint of their advanced technology and intelligence might  have been an interesting contrast to the rest of the visuals of the movie. Speaking of which, the production design is staggering in its detail to reproduce an authentic medieval experience.  Again, it feels like the filmmakers shot on location in the Middle Ages, which is an incredible feat in and of itself.

Não demora muito para que, vendo É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS (2013), a gente desista logo de entender a trama e se permita viajar na força onírica de suas imagens. Há quem diga que é porque o livro no qual o filme é baseado é de difícil adaptação, mas é possível que o cineasta russo Aleksey German não tenha se preocupado muito com esse tipo de detalhe. Seu filme-testamento, em nenhum momento, procura ser fácil para o espectador, foi feito como que numa delírio. O fato de ter quase três horas de duração também não ajuda muito o trabalho a ser apreciado por espectadores apressados e impacientes. É preciso paciência e uma reeducação do olhar para que essas imagens poderosas sejam não só apreciadas, mas recebidas com maravilhamento e assombro, misturado também a algum asco provocado por cenas violentas ou de causar repulsa mesmo, como pessoas com o nariz pingando, com feridas expostas ou imagens de cadáveres pendurados ou vísceras à mostra, num espetáculo tão perturbador que esquece-se que são efeitos especiais. Talvez o preto e branco das imagens passe essa impressão de verdade. É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS é um dos trabalhos mais importantes da carreira de German, contemporâneo de Andrei Tarkovski, e que morreu antes de ver sua obra finalizada. German passou quatro décadas idealizando, doze anos filmando e faleceu em 2013, deixando a edição e a finalização para seu filho e sua esposa, ambos colaboradores de longa data da produção. Felizmente é um desses trabalhos bem especiais, que oferecem ao espectador uma experiência única, que vai além do gostar ou do não gostar. Independentemente disso, saímos da sessão diferentes. É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS se passa em um universo semelhante à nossa Idade Média em alguns países da Europa, mas há algo de muito estranho que nos leva a acreditar que se trata de um mundo novo e estranho. E na verdade se trata de um outro planeta, como é dito no início, nos letreiros de apresentação. Ver o filme no cinema ou ao menos em uma tela maior é essencial para que os vários planos gerais e os ricos detalhes da direção de arte e a bela fotografia em preto e branco sejam vistos com mais clareza. É, definitivamente, um filme para ser assistido no cinema, por mais difícil que seja sua exibição comercial. Tanto é que até agora ele permanece inédito em nosso circuito. Pude vê-lo em uma mostra dedicada a filmes ousados esteticamente e arriscados comercialmente, a Mostra Cinema em Transe, exibida em Fortaleza no mês de janeiro. O curioso de ler a sinopse de É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS é não encontrar exatamente o que é descrito na tela. Na trama, um grupo de cientistas é enviado ao planeta Arkanar para ajudar a civilização local, que está passando por uma fase ainda muito rudimentar de sua história, a encontrar o seu caminho para o progresso. A missão é difícil, já que eles não podem interferir violentamente e nem matar aquelas pessoas. O cientista Rumata tenta salvar os intelectuais locais de uma punição. Essa é mais ou menos a sinopse meio maluca e resumida que aparece no IMDB. Na confusa história que acompanhamos na tela, que é o que importa, afinal, já que a obra cinematográfica precisa ser analisada de modo independente da obra literária, vemos um homem de aparência quase gigante e considerado um deus pelos demais. Aos nossos olhos ele só parece superior aos demais por ser maior, mais forte, se vestir diferente e principalmente por não estar coberto de lama. Os demais mais parecem porcos vivendo em um chiqueiro. A lama é uma constante e está presente em quase todo o filme. Ainda que adaptado da obra literária dos mestres da ficção científica russa Arkady e Boris Strugatsky, que também serviram de inspiração para uma das obras mais aclamadas de Tarkovski, STALKER, o filme de German brinca muito com as possibilidades que só o cinema é capaz, como a aproximação um tanto exagerada da câmera nos rostos e corpos dos atores, ou a própria maneira como eles lidam com essa câmera, chegando, em alguns momentos, a falar com ela. É o tipo de obra que cobra muito do espectador, mas que recompensa muito bem aqueles dispostos a irem até o fim em sua difícil travessia. I remember sitting on my friends dorm room floor and buying this for 4 dollars nearly a decade ago. Ever since then it has been on my Mount Everest of films alongside the act of killing and an elephant sitting still, films that I know I need to watch but are extremely difficult and grueling. I’m still not sure if I like this film, but I really loved the themes and imagery. Given that the director spent decades trying to make this in Soviet Russia, it brilliantly shows how rampant ant-intellectualism will ultimately lead a society to live in a world filled with piss, shit, blood, mud, spit, snot, and an overall grime that makes you as nihilistic as the main character. The audio design was incredible and if I recall correctly, the entire film is dubbed audio, making all of the disgusting noises of mud and dripping water even more unnerving. Before last night I had probably tried to watch this more than a dozen times. This leads me to my main criticism: despite having watched the first ~90 minutes so many times, I still had no idea what was going on. This film isn’t for everyone, but it is an unforgettable experience.

Если "Хрусталев, машину!" магнум опус Алексея Юрьевича, то "Трудно быть богом" фильм его мечты, который режиссер пытался реализовать, только вдумайтесь с 1968 года. Прошло целых 46 лет с написания первого травта сценария до выхода фильма на экраны России. Перед просмотром решил я ознакомится с оригинальной повестью братьев Стругацких и правильно сделал. Для Германа сюжет второстепенен, иногда он будто специально мешает ему развиваться, прерывая важные диалоги из книги всякими бесмылсеными, но придающими атмосферу "жестами", а потому без знания исходного сюжета понять происходящее по отрывкам, хоть и можно, но сложно. Здесь главный герой вовсе не Дон Румата, а Арканар, грязный мерзкий вызывающий отвращение, мир лишённой культуры, где обитатели в основном тупые уроды с садистскими наклонностями и что самое страшное, даже земляни, которые казалось бы должны нести свет в этот мрак приспособились и стали напоминать местных обитателей. В фильме есть одно добавление к повести, которое может показаться малозначительным, но на самом деле оно очень важно: У Руматы было 270 дуэлей в рамках которых не один человек не умер, но всем своим противникам он отрубал уши (последнего уточнения, как раз таки и не было в повести), причем в картине благородный Дон не раз напоминает людям о своем таланте отрубать ухо, словно, хвастаясь им. Кроме того, если в повести Румата не убивает больше из морального принципа, тут же стойкое ощущение, что  лишь из-за правил он пытается не допустить смерть, а дай ему волю... Герман намеренно делал фильм в разы мрачнее оригинала, его можно интерпретировать как предостережение человечеству. Режиссер демонстрирует, что будет с людьми без культуры, мир превратится в ад воплоти. А с помощью уникальнейшего киноязыка Алексей Герман добивается полного погружения зрителя в фильм, послевкусия от такого очень сильное, после просмотра мне даже казалось, что я будто и правда побывал в Арканаре, а может там и остался.  Сны были соответствующими. "Трудно быть богом", безусловно великое кино, которое уверен эстеты будут обсуждать и через 50 лет.

An absolutely singular vision of a pseudo-middle ages wallowing in the abject. Every scene is jam packed with bodies and objects covered in shit and piss and blood and snot and viscera. It's absolutely, disgustingly, filthy. And we are the omniscient observer of it all, incapable of changing it and refusing to look away. Frequently the actors will look straight down the barrel of the camera and break the fourth wall by engaging with the viewer. Sometimes they'll do a little dance, or show their ass, and sometimes they look at the viewer challenging us as if we are the depraved. Why are we looking at them? What is wrong with us that we want to see these people living in this filth? I think there's also a pretty obvious message about a world that rejects knowledge. That the culture that develops in such a place descends to the most base level of depravity, superstition, ignorance, and violence. This is a place easily duped by a charismatic man who can swagger his way around town, and maybe swing a sword better than most. And what does it get them in the end? Absolutely nothing good. It's a rough watch, especially at fucking 3 hours long. It's a meandering mess of a narrative, but it's also a spectacle of filth and a hell of an achievement.

Hard to Be a God takes you through a world where people look directly into the camera and objects are constantly dangled in front of it, while faces and hands appear from nowhere like the lens is another person trying to make its way through each brutal scene. I absolutely love it and these are some Sunday morning ramblings as to why. The main character, Rumata, goes through a constant bombardment of requests and threats, alongside the filth and brutality of the society he is in. But for most of the film he takes almost everything in his stride, like he's super calm regardless of what mess is happening. He knows another kind of civilisation is possible and knows that something needs to change, but that doesn't mean he can do anything on his own. So he's kind of stuck in a perpetual cycle of guts and grime; back and forth with piss, snot and puddles and random machines and spikes and musical instruments and fog. But in spite of that, I never felt the film lacked 'progress' because I never really got why 'progress' needs to mean moving in a tidy way from one point to another. Life doesn't really work that way, or maybe it does for some folks, but it doesn't for social and technological development, despite how we might think that it does. Rumata basically continues living in this world where everything is interrupted and familiar problems return, with the Renaissance he knows could happen staying somewhere on the horizon beyond the moonshine, zits and donkey penises. The filthiness is probably pushed a bit too far, and 3 hours of hawking and traipsing through sludge, alongside lacerated butt cheeks and dead fish, totally becomes an endurance test - but that was also part of the fun. I didn't find it repetitive because the filmmaker finds so many different ways of presenting this world, particularly through the movement of the camera and the awesome use of props. It is disgusting and obscene, but it also has moments of despair and grief for characters whose lives I got interested in without necessarily identifying with them. The Baron, for instance, waving his sword around like a raging loon before ending up face down with arrows in his back was especially brutal. He had so much more to give! The film also left me thinking about a society where few people seem capable of imagining that things could be different, while Rumata knows that they can be and still can't work out how to make that change happen. His knowledge and his $$$ distinguishes him from the people around him, but he's not really superior cos he still spits and flings donkey poop, increasingly behaving like someone who belongs in that time and place. The thing that makes him different is that he knows another world is possible, while the film gradually tests how much that knowledge is worth when he can't create it himself. By the time he goes berserk and loses his restraint, the hours beforehand validate his spree, and I found the whole thing fascinating and totally unforgettable.

Que filme absurdo. Definitivamente dificil e longe de ser pra qualquer um, 2 horas e 50 minutos passeando na lama e de alguma forma eu me senti em um transe, olhando pela janela. Não só uma viagem a um planeta medieval como eu esperava, mas uma viagem ao planeta dominado pela idiocracia. Um planeta que abraçou sua idade das trevas, fadado a estar eternamente abraçado na ignorância. A renascença não aconteceu, e nem qualquer ideia de progresso social ou artistico acontecerá. O intelectualismo e o bom uso do ofício foi caçado a extinção. Um grande pessimismo de uma estagnação sistemática da humanidade e do progresso social comparado ao próprio planeta Arkanar. Vindo frustrado de uma união soviética complexa, parece que o diretor Aleksei German fez esse filme (que foi o grande trabalho da sua vida, tendo morrido até antes de termina-lo) uma grande ode ao fracasso social. Não só ao modelo soviético, mas como ao que se segue, que fracassou e segue fracassando e talvez eternamente fracassará. Apesar de claramente demonstrar todo seu amargor ao decaimento soviético, a ponta da espada que ele aponta parece ser direcionada a toda e qualquer ideia de renovação social, onde líderes não mais importam e nenhuma tentativa revolucionária pode funcionar, o tecido social ja está impregnado pela mediocridade. A obsessão pela auto-destruição social é clara. Aos 15 minutos de filme um camponês olha para a camera após ouvir uma colmeia e diz sorridente "as abelhas estão matando sua rainha", e desde então o tema não saiu da minha cabeça. O protagonista como impotente observador é o artista frustrado ao perceber que nada nunca vai mudar. A falencia social nao é um evento ou um momento de Arkanar, é uma doença que rasteja desde o lamaçal medieval até hoje. É vírus que viaja de sarcofagos aos motores que levaram Rumata até as terras da miséria. No livro adaptado, a terra se estabeleceu em uma utopia comunista e que eventualmente leva o homem até os planetas simulacros à terra, presos no passado. Fica claro que a ideia narrativa é o pessimismo de que mesmo se realmente encontramos o caminho sistemático pra nossa especie, nossa anti-renascença aconteceu, não precisa mais existir lordes que comandam o expurgo do progresso, ele é automatizado pela humanidade. É perceptível o esmero que foi entregue a cada cena e porque demorou tantos anos a ser feito. Cada quadro é absurdo e com tanta textura que me deu vontade de tomar um banho depois. A cinegrafia é como se Hieronymus Bosch tivesse uma câmera, ele com certeza estaria mirando na mesma direção que Aleksei German mira. O som é grotesco e visceral, e muitas vezes alto demais ou tendo o diálogo desconexo da cena, me pergunto se ele tivesse tido tempo de terminar ainda soaria assim. Mas a camera incessante é um dos melhores aspectos da direção, nem sempre pela continuidade da cena em si mas pelo seu movimento, esbarrando em moradores, buscando as cenas curiosa. Toda vez que um morador miserável olhava pra câmera eu não sentia que a quarta parede estava quebrando, e sim que eu estava ali andando na lama e não paravam de me olhar com curiosidade, de certa forma eu estava fadado a ser um observador assim como Rumata, assim como todos nós que já adentramos nossa anti-renascença. Aleksei German’s final film, Trudno byt bogom (Hard to Be a God), is a filthy, furious masterpiece, reminiscent of the grotesqueries we find in François Rabelais’ pentalogy La vie de Gargantua et de Pantagruel and in the paintings of Bruegel and Bosch. Together with cinematographers Vladimir Ilin and Yuriy Klimenko, German depicts a grim, chilly, decaying medieval society. Based on a novel by the Strugatsky Brothers, the film features an excellent performance by Leonid Yarmolnik, who moves through the claustrophobic scenery like a disordered Don Quixote. Trudno byt bogom is demanding in every sense of the word. It is a transgressive, grotesque spectacle like no other - an insistent, intrusive, and steadfast piece of cinema. Its humid, squelching, hellish visions, extreme close-ups, and brutal events all contribute to the film’s darkly bizarre style. At times, the dwelling camerawork comes at the expense of narrative development, but Trudno byt bogom remains an impressive and utterly unique experience.

What a masterpiece. There’s more than half a million movies out there but nothing will ever come close to this. Aleksei Germans adaption of the Strugatsky brothers sciencefiction book “H ard to be a God ” is a cinematic milestone. This is one of those films that completely disregards conventional storytelling. It’s super unorthodox. Random medieval peasants walking in frame, looking you dead in the eyes, and continuing their way. This movie makes you feel like YOURE the cameraman that films this documentary of the gross and ugly medieval world that is Arkanar, and everyone there has never seen a camera before… Somehow this bizarre approach only makes the world feel more authentic. You’re not watching this world from a distance, you’re living in it. The cinematography are astonishing. Every frame is full of detail. Mud, rain, smoke, bodies, animals, snot, those medieval peasants… it somehow manages to be beautiful and repulsive at the same time. This movie can be extremely gory at times though. Yuck. The amount of practical effects on display is unbelievable. I genuinely don’t know how Aleksei German managed to do this, it feels like a real civilization that has existed for centuries. What got to me most was the underlying story. We follow Rumata, a scientist from earth, who’s seen as a God by the people from Arkanar. His goal was to study the planet, but his heart tells him to instead help this planet progress out of the medieval times. Only thing is, earths code is to not interfere, kill or change the history of this planet. He sees how instead of transitioning into a renaissance, this civilization actually slips backwards due to a fascist, anti-intellectualism regime that kills off everyone that practices any form of free thinking. Art, writing, science, etc. It gets more difficult for Rumata not to interfere. Especially when people close to him are getting killed by this regime. The title “ Hard to Be a God ” becomes increasingly more meaningful as the film progresses, and I absolutely love the way this message is implemented. I can understand why this film isn’t for everyone. At times it’s exhausting, overwhelming, gory and almost impossible to follow. But I believe that’s exactly what Aleksei German intended. At first I didn’t like the constant filth, strange dialogue and chaotic camerawork. It felt like sensory overload. But as the movie progressed, I actually came to love these traits. It really adds to the experience. A film unlike anything I’ve ever seen. One that I’ll probably appreciate even more after a couple rewatches.
